title: Sharabhanga
hook: a king of the gods is visiting an old sage, and when Rama walks up, the god leaves

segments.voice: Yesterday: Viradha, part two. The giant turned out to be a cursed musician, rose free from the pit, and sent the brothers to a sage. Did you wonder about the story under someone's behavior? Day five hundred fifty-five.

Rama follows Viradha's directions, and as they near Sharabhanga's hermitage, he stops. There's a chariot in the air above the clearing, blazing like the sun, pulled by green horses. A white umbrella shades the figure standing in it, and attendants crowd around. Rama tells Lakshmana: that's Indra, king of the gods, talking with the sage. And then, as the brothers walk closer, Indra says something to his companions, and the chariot rises and goes.
screen: `A CHARIOT ABOVE THE CLEARING.` → `INDRA, KING OF THE GODS.` → `HE LEAVES AS RAMA COMES.`

segments.voice: Why does Indra leave? Valmiki gives him a reason, spoken to the people around him. Rama is coming, he says, and I shouldn't meet him yet. He has work to do first. When it's done, I'll see him. The text is hinting at what lies ahead: a war that the gods themselves need Rama to fight. But it doesn't tell us more, and it doesn't need to. The god of storms and rain stepping aside for a man in bark clothes is the point. Rama goes in, and Sharabhanga, very old, welcomes him. Indra came to take me to Brahma's world, he says. I've earned it by my austerities. But I heard you were near, and I wouldn't leave until I had seen my guest. Then the old sage makes an extraordinary offer. All the worlds I've won by my tapas, all that merit, I give it to you. Take it. And Rama says no, kindly. I'll earn my own worlds, he says. Just tell me where in this forest I should live. That's a small, sharp moment. A free gift of heaven, from someone who means it, and Rama turns it down, not out of pride but because he has his own road to walk. Sharabhanga accepts that, and tells him to go to Sutikshna, another sage further on. But before Rama goes, Sharabhanga asks him to stay a little longer and watch. He has one last thing to do.
screen: `I SHOULDN'T MEET HIM YET.` · `I WAITED TO SEE MY GUEST.` · `TAKE ALL MY MERIT.` · `I'LL EARN MY OWN WORLDS.` · then, large: `A GIFT OF HEAVEN, DECLINED.`

segments.voice: Sit with your hands open on your knees. Think of something you're working toward, slowly, a skill, a habit, a repair in a relationship. If there's a wish that someone would just hand it to you finished, notice it. Now picture yourself taking the next small step on your own feet. Feel the weight of your body on the seat, your own weight, carrying you. Breathe steadily with that. The bell holds the time.
Sharabhanga. The old sage who waited to see Rama before going to heaven, and offered him all his merit, which Rama kindly declined.
Your line: Sharabhanga. Today, take one step on something you'd rather someone else did for you. Day five hundred fifty-five.

howItsDone: In the text, Indra withdraws before meeting Rama, and some devotees read the scene as the gods waiting on Rama's mission.

fork.setup: you're Rama. a great sage offers you all the heavenly worlds he has earned. what do you say?
options: ask him to give them to your father.
fork.reveal: Rama declines kindly, and asks only where he should live. Sharabhanga sends him to Sutikshna.

original.note: Sanskrit śarabhaṅga: the name of the old sage of Dandaka who waits to see Rama.

trapdoor: what you thought: the sage is just one more hermit on the way.
what it means: he has delayed heaven itself to see Rama, and offers it to him.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 5 has Indra withdraw because Rama's task isn't done, an early hint of the war the gods are waiting for.
